signals.name: Silver
signals.label: Gives back Monday's bounce: -2% to ~$57.5 on a firmer dollar into the FOMC
signals.detail: Silver spot ~$57.5 (-2%, Tue 28 Jul); gold ~$4,030; GDX ~$75.4 (YTD ~-12%)
signals.takeaway: The single most important line item for this book whipsawed straight back down: silver fell ~2% to ~$57.5 on Tuesday, reversing Monday's rebound to ~$59.4, as a firmer dollar and pre-FOMC de-risking overrode the oil relief and the Iran de-escalation stripped out the geopolitical bid. Silver is 2-3x more rate-sensitive than gold, so it gave back most into the 29 Jul decision. Structural deficit thesis holds (Silver Institute 6th straight annual deficit; JPMorgan ~$81 avg); treat the FOMC as the next binary — hedge the silver-vs-gold spread into the print rather than chasing bounces with added leverage.

signals.name: Crude oil / Energy
signals.label: Oil keeps sliding as the Iran pause holds; Brent ~$84, Iran opens Hormuz talks
signals.detail: Brent -4.8% to ~$84.09, WTI -4% to ~$79.26 (Tue 28 Jul); US-Iran pause holds; Iran in Hormuz talks with Saudi/Oman
signals.takeaway: The US-Iran war had been the dominant cross-portfolio driver, and the de-escalation held and extended — the strike pause held into a further session and Iran opened Strait-of-Hormuz talks with Saudi Arabia and Oman — deflating the oil premium further (a sharp reversal of last week's spike to Brent ~$102). That is a net positive for the far-larger rate-sensitive book (levered silver, S-REITs, HK tech, crypto) at the cost of the small energy long, though it also removed the safe-haven bid under metals. Iran denied a reported 10-day ceasefire, so trade the pause-holds-vs-breaks-down odds; the Red Sea/Yemen front is the residual escalation risk keeping a floor under oil.

signals.name: US Treasuries / rates
signals.label: Fed decides 29 Jul: hawkish hold base case, hike odds ~1-in-3; 10Y eases to ~4.62%
signals.detail: CME hike odds ~34-36%; Sept hike odds ~80%; 10Y ~4.62% (from ~4.71%); decision Wed 29 Jul 2pm ET, no SEP
signals.takeaway: The dominant macro headwind for the book's highest-beta pain (levered silver, gold miners) and for S-REITs stays higher-for-longer, but the oil slide eased the 10Y back to ~4.62% (from a year-high ~4.71%). CME hike odds are ~1-in-3 into the 29 Jul decision, though September odds hold near 80%. Chair Warsh's hawkish, no-guidance regime removes the cushion of forward-guided cuts. The big USD cash pile earns ~3.5-3.75% as productive dry powder for a post-FOMC metals shakeout; a dovish 29 Jul surprise or a durable Iran de-escalation is the upside catalyst, a hawkish hold or hike the downside.

signals.name: Gold / gold miners
signals.label: Slips ~-1.25% to ~$4,030 pre-FOMC as the dollar firms; drew largest fund inflow since April
signals.detail: Gold ~$4,030 (-1.25%, Tue 28 Jul), below $4,100 and the ~$4,130 two-week high; gold funds +$2.0bn (wk to 22 Jul)
signals.takeaway: Gold gave back ground alongside silver as a firmer dollar and pre-FOMC de-risking took over — but it held far better than silver and drew the largest weekly gold-fund inflow since April (+$2.0bn), with multi-month central-bank buying providing a structural floor. Favor the gold-heavy miners (GDX) over pure silver leverage as the steadier way to hold metals exposure; but BofA's 'death cross' and elevated net-longs are the near-term warning, and a hawkish Fed could fade gold toward $4,000. The ~$4,130 high is the level to reclaim.

signals.name: Rare earths (ex-China basket)
signals.label: Malaysia probes Lynas-Pentagon deal; MP's DoD floor vs China controls suspended to Nov
signals.detail: Malaysian committee scrutinizes Lynas's US$96M DoD supply deal ($110/kg NdPr floor); China controls suspended to 10 Nov, magnet exports 6-mo high
signals.takeaway: The China/US rare-earth decoupling structurally favors the ex-China watchlist (MP — DoD ~15% stake + $110/kg NdPr floor; Lynas — record cash; Energy Fuels — White Mesa NdPr build-out), reinforced by Trump's 20 Jul EO barring adversary-sourced critical materials. But a Malaysian parliamentary committee is now probing Lynas's US DoD supply deal — a political overhang on its Malaysian processing base — and China's export controls are suspended to 10 Nov (magnet exports +75% MoM), easing near-term pricing urgency. This is a strategic optionality play on the controls snapping back after 10 Nov, not an immediate momentum trade — accumulate MP and government-backed UUUU on weakness into that catalyst.

signals.name: Singapore blue-chips / S-REITs
signals.label: SGX REIT season opens strong (Keppel DC REIT DPU +11.3%); STI banks drag Tuesday; DBS 6 Aug
signals.detail: Keppel DC REIT 1H26 DPU +11.3% to 5.714c; STI -0.35% Tue as banks drag (DBS ~S$73.95); Singtel S$2B buyback; DBS reports 6 Aug (guided FY26 lower), CapLand Ascendas REIT 5 Aug
signals.takeaway: SGX REIT reporting opened strong — Keppel DC REIT posted 1H26 distributable income +18.5% y/y and DPU +11.3%, a constructive read-through for the S-REIT sleeve (Keppel REIT, Mapletree PACT), and an easing rate path (oil down, 10Y ~4.62%) would relieve the whole sleeve. But the STI slipped ~0.35% Tuesday as banks dragged on global weakness, DBS has guided FY2026 profit slightly below 2025, and the China-retail drag persists (CapLand China Trust FY25 DPU -14.7%). Singtel's S$2B value-realisation buyback is a structural bid under a core holding. A reported (unconfirmed) MAS move to a single S-REIT leverage cap is worth verifying before repositioning the REIT holdings; watch DBS results 6 Aug.

signals.name: Tencent / HK tech
signals.label: Internet giants firm despite the chip rout; record China inflow (+$21.3bn) under the Politburo signal
signals.detail: Hang Seng +0.41% (4th straight gain), HS Tech +0.61% Tue as Tencent/Alibaba/Xiaomi anchor vs SMIC/semis giving back gains; China drew a record 3rd-largest weekly equity inflow (+$21.3bn)
signals.takeaway: The HK-tech core's internet names decoupled from the global chip rout — the Hang Seng rose a 4th straight session with Tencent, Alibaba and Xiaomi anchoring even as SMIC/semis sold off on the NVDA $250B-OpenAI-backstop scare (KOSPI circuit-breaker, Nikkei -4.4%). The 24 Jul Politburo's stronger-than-expected stimulus language is now being confirmed by flows: China drew a record 3rd-largest weekly equity inflow (+$21.3bn), the biggest MLF injection in five months. Favor Tencent/Xiaomi (internet/consumer) over the SMIC chip leg while the AI-capex/memory unwind runs; watch Tencent's 12 Aug results and August policy follow-through. US risk-off and a hawkish Fed are the near-term beta headwinds.

congress.rationale: The California Democrat sold Nvidia (disclosed 27 Jul) — trimming into the late-July NVDA ~5% pullback and the AI-financing/circular-funding scare that triggered the global chip rout.
congress.deepDive: A fresh, well-timed de-risk from the semis leader just as the AI-capex-peak narrative deepened (NVDA's reported ~$250B OpenAI backstop, KOSPI circuit-breaker, Nikkei -4.4%). Sits opposite the Micron/AI bulls (Newhouse) and validates Burry's standing chip shorts — the congressional book splitting on the AI-capex debate. A direct read-through to the SMIC chip leg of the HK-tech core.

congress.rationale: The Florida Democrat bought a healthcare + mega-cap-AI basket (HCA, META, MSFT, AMAT, HD, plus pre-IPO SpaceX) and sold S&P Global, disclosed 27 Jul — leaning into defensives + AI-infrastructure into the FOMC/earnings week.
congress.deepDive: A diversified rotation into the mega-cap AI complex (META/MSFT/AMAT) paired with a healthcare defensive (HCA) and a private-market SpaceX allocation — a barbell that mirrors the model's XLV lean and the crowded AI-infra longs (Ackman/Bridgewater). Lands the same day as Liccardo's NVDA sell, capturing the two-sided AI-capex debate within Congress.

congress.representative: Nancy Pelosi (Paul Pelosi / PFP Family Office)
congress.rationale: Newly disclosed late-July PTR shows the Pelosi household bought long-dated Intel (INTC) and Uber (UBER) call options on 29 May, together worth up to ~$6M — a leveraged bullish bet, with the Intel calls a play on the US semiconductor-reshoring/CHIPS tailwind and possible government support for INTC.
congress.deepDive: The most-watched congressional book: deep in-the-money LEAP calls are Paul Pelosi's signature structure and have front-run large tech moves before. The Intel leg lands as INTC restructures under state/government-backstop chatter; the Uber leg extends the household's mega-cap tech/mobility tilt. Disclosed ~two months after execution (within the 45-day STOCK Act window from filing). No direct overlap with the metals/HK/SGX book, but a high-signal smart-money tell on US semis.

congress.rationale: The Michigan Democrat bought Freddie Mac (traded 14 Jul, freshly disclosed) — a speculative bet amid renewed GSE-privatization chatter under the administration.
congress.deepDive: One of the freshest dated Democratic disclosures this window and a rare GSE/housing-finance play among congressional books, tied to the on-again talk of releasing Fannie/Freddie from conservatorship. High-idiosyncratic-risk single name, minimal overlap with the portfolio.

congress.rationale: The Pennsylvania Republican bought Snowflake and Veeva (data/AI and life-sciences cloud), funded by sells in Guidewire, Arista, Okta and McDonald's — a rotation into data/AI software.
congress.deepDive: A fresh single-member rotation into AI-data infrastructure just as the broader tape de-rated semis on AI-capex doubt — a bet on the software/data layer over the chip layer. Bresnahan is among the more active House traders; funded by trimming higher-multiple software and a consumer name.

congress.rationale: The Louisiana Democrat bought Nvidia (up to ~$45K) on AI/chip momentum — among the Democratic tech buyers flagged by Unusual Whales, the opposite side of Whitehouse's June trim.
congress.deepDive: The split NVDA views across members (Fields buying, Whitehouse selling) capture the market's own AI-capex debate. Lands just as the House passed a bill (22 Jul) to bar members from trading individual stocks — a backdrop worth watching for the whole congressional-trade signal.

congress.rationale: The Kansas Republican senator bought Berkshire Hathaway B shares (traded 23 Jun, disclosed ~21 Jul), pairing it with an Alphabet add — a conservative blue-chip pairing.
congress.deepDive: Notable as it echoes Berkshire's own GOOGL build under Greg Abel; a low-turnover, quality tilt from a senator into the post-Buffett era.

congress.rationale: Added Alphabet (traded 23 Jun, disclosed ~21 Jul) alongside the Berkshire buy — Alphabet AI exposure.
congress.deepDive: Alphabet is one of the most widely-owned names across both Congress and the tracked super-investors (Berkshire tripled it in Q1); a consensus quality-AI holding.

congress.rationale: The New Jersey Republican bought Wheaton Precious Metals (silver/gold streamer) alongside EQT (nat-gas) and ESAB (industrials), disclosed 17 Jul — a hard-asset/energy tilt.
congress.deepDive: The single most on-theme congressional trade for this book — a member adding a precious-metals streamer into the silver run, paired with nat-gas exposure into the oil shock. A rare direct overlap with the portfolio's PM-miner sleeve.

congress.rationale: Bought EQT (natural gas) in the same 17 Jul-disclosed basket — an energy add into the Iran-war oil premium.
congress.deepDive: Nat-gas leverage lines up with the energy-capex/inflation theme driving the tape; funded partly by sells in GOOGL, JNJ and MKL (a rebalance).

congress.rationale: The Washington Republican bought Micron (memory) along with FirstEnergy and Uber, disclosed 20 Jul — a rotation into memory/utilities/mobility.
congress.deepDive: The Micron add contrasts with Burry's fresh MU short — the AI-storage-cycle bull case vs the chip-peak bear case now playing out across smart-money books. Funded by sells in GOOGL, CSX and ADBE.

congress.rationale: The Texas Republican bought Meta (via options) plus a leveraged-crude product (USOU), disclosed 17 Jul — a Meta-upside + oil-leverage combination.
congress.deepDive: The leveraged-crude add is a direct bet on the Iran-war oil premium; paired against sells in GOOG, AMZN and AAPL (mega-cap-tech profit-taking). An active, thematic trader.

congress.rationale: The Connecticut Democrat sold Bank of America alongside Home Depot and Exxon, disclosed 21 Jul — trimming banks, retail and energy.
congress.deepDive: A broad de-risk across cyclicals (financials/retail/energy) by a senior House Financial Services member; notable as it lightens exactly the rate/consumer-sensitive names most exposed to a higher-for-longer Fed.

congress.rationale: Sold Exxon in the same 21 Jul-disclosed basket — an energy trim even as the Iran war lifted oil.
congress.deepDive: A contrarian energy sale into the war premium — either profit-taking after a run or a de-escalation call; part of a broad cyclical de-risk.

congress.rationale: The Georgia Republican exited Intuit, disclosed 16 Jul — a single-name software trim.
congress.deepDive: A clean exit from a high-multiple software name into the AI-capex-doubt window; consistent with the broader rotation out of expensive growth.

congress.rationale: The Alabama senator sold Lockheed Martin inside a broad basket liquidation (AWK, CSX, DUK, MA, NEE, PFE), disclosed 16 Jul — winding down holdings as a gubernatorial candidate.
congress.deepDive: A contrarian defense trim into a hot geopolitical backdrop, part of a wholesale basket sell tied to his campaign — notable given Tuberville is among Congress's most active traders.

congress.rationale: The Florida Republican sold Nokia and Bank of America (plus GE options), disclosed 20 Jul — exiting telecom and a bank.
congress.deepDive: Another member lightening financials into the higher-for-longer backdrop; the BAC sale echoes Himes's same-week bank trim.

congress.rationale: Disclosed a very large, months-late basket (700+ trades, mix of buys/sells across PFE, HON, HD, RACE, FDX, DVN and more) on 22 Jul — flagged by Unusual Whales as a STOCK Act late-filing.
congress.deepDive: A newly-active filer disclosed a sprawling, diversified basket well past the 45-day window; notable mainly for the scale and the late filing rather than a single directional signal — a broad, cyclically-tilted rebalance.

congress.rationale: The Rhode Island Democrat trimmed Nvidia (up to ~$250K, also traded AAPL and MU) at elevated AI valuations — a well-timed sell of the market's most-owned AI name.
congress.deepDive: Echoes Burry's fresh chip shorts and the opposite side of Fields's NVDA buy; the split congressional views mirror the market's live AI-capex debate.

congress.rationale: An executive-branch official disclosed buying the 'NANC' Democratic-congressional-trades ETF — copying Democratic congressional trades via a fund (a notable exec-branch PTR).
congress.deepDive: A meta-signal on the congressional-trading theme itself: an official buying the ETF that mechanically tracks Democratic members' disclosed trades, into a week when the House voted to ban members from trading individual stocks.

superInvestors.name: Scion / Michael Burry (personal)
superInvestors.rationale: Having deregistered Scion in late 2025, Burry now trades personally and discloses via Substack — around 25 July 2026 he EXPANDED the chip-short book to NVDA, MU, AMAT, SOXX, TSLA and CAT (via puts), arguing hyperscalers are extending GPU depreciation schedules and that a write-down/order-cut cycle is coming — 'the beginning of the end' of the chip boom.
superInvestors.deepDive: These are his freshest, most public bets and they kept working into the late-July AI-capex rout — NVDA fell to ~$193 (-6% on the week) by 28 Jul as an NVDA ~$250B OpenAI-backstop report triggered a global chip sell-off (KOSPI circuit-breaker, Nikkei -4.4%). The cleanest smart-money expression of the AI-capex-peak thesis in the tape, directly opposite the Micron/AI buys in some congressional books (Newhouse) and the crowded AI-infra longs (Ackman/Tepper/Bridgewater). No 13F any longer — the Substack is the only window; self-reported posts, sizes approximate, not SEC filings.

superInvestors.name: Berkshire Hathaway
superInvestors.value: AAPL+GOOGL now ~30% of a ~$348B equity book
superInvestors.rationale: Under Greg Abel, Berkshire has loaded up on Alphabet (roughly $10B cash deployed), lifting Apple + Alphabet to ~30% of the ~$348B equity book, and resumed buybacks in March after a ~21-month pause — Barron's estimates ~$5-11B repurchased in Q2 (inferred from Buffett's annual-donation filing).
superInvestors.deepDive: The Alphabet build plus the buyback restart signal Abel is willing to trade actively even as Buffett sits on a record cash pile (~$397B at Q1-end); analysts expect a 15th straight net-selling quarter in Q2, so the Alphabet add sits against continued net equity sales. The $9.7B OxyChem acquisition (its biggest buy since 2022) closed 2 Jan. A striking contrast with Duquesne's Q1 GOOGL exit. Q2 13F due 14 Aug — confirm the GOOGL size and the sell-streak then.

superInvestors.name: Pershing Square
superInvestors.rationale: Bill Ackman raised Pershing's Howard Hughes stake to ~46.9% earlier this cycle while building a 'modern Berkshire'; his Q1 13F (filed 15 May) added a new ~$2.09B Microsoft stake (~15% of book) and exited Hilton, Chipotle and CP Kansas City — top holds now Brookfield (~17.6%), Amazon (~17.4%), Uber (~15.7%), Microsoft (~15.3%), Restaurant Brands (~12.2%). He has teased four new (undisclosed) positions already in the funds for the Q2 report.
superInvestors.deepDive: The HHH build anchors his holding-company vision; the new MSFT stake, the four teased positions and the Pershing Square USA IPO prep make his 14 Aug 13F one of the most-watched of the cycle. Amazon remains a crowded whale consensus (also top for Tepper). No fresh activist 13D surfaced this run.

superInvestors.name: Appaloosa
superInvestors.rationale: David Tepper's Q1 book (filed 15 May, ~$5.93B / 31 positions) is led by Amazon (~15%), Micron (~9.5%), Alphabet, Uber and TSM; he exited most bank stocks and added heavily to memory (Micron). No July 13D/13G surfaced — carried pending the 14 Aug Q2 13F.
superInvestors.deepDive: Tepper's Amazon conviction makes it the single most-consensus mega-cap long across the tracked whales (also top for Ackman) — a crowded position now exposed to the AI-growth wobble; the big Micron weight sits directly opposite Burry's fresh MU short.

superInvestors.name: Duquesne Family Office
superInvestors.rationale: Stanley Druckenmiller exited Alphabet entirely and opened a new Broadcom stake while adding SanDisk, Seagate and Micron across 31 new positions and 23 exits in Q1; top holding Natera (~18%). Nothing new verified mid-cycle.
superInvestors.deepDive: High-turnover repositioning that leans into AI-storage/semis (AVGO/SNDK/STX/MU) while dropping GOOGL — a sharp contrast with Berkshire's ~$10B Alphabet build and a mixed read on the AI trade into the July semis wobble.

superInvestors.name: Tiger Global
superInvestors.rationale: Chase Coleman added TSM (+49%), Applied Materials (+85%), Broadcom (+25%), Meta (+12%) and Nvidia in Q1; top holdings GOOGL (~$4.2B), NVDA (~$2.8B), AMZN (~$2.6B). No verifiable mid-cycle move this run.
superInvestors.deepDive: Tiger leaned hard into the AI-semis supply chain in Q1 — a stance now tested by the July AI-capex-doubt drawdown and Burry's chip shorts. Carried pending the 14 Aug 13F.

superInvestors.name: Soros Fund Management
superInvestors.rationale: George Soros's fund held an S&P 500 put as its top position ($773M) and added NVDA, TSM and EA while cutting Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft in Q1 — a hedged, cautious posture. No new 13D/13G surfaced mid-cycle.
superInvestors.deepDive: The large index-put top holding is a portfolio hedge rather than a directional short, but it captures the defensive tilt among some whales into a stretched tape — a useful read into the late-July rate/metals stress. Q2 13F due 14 Aug.

superInvestors.name: Gates Foundation Trust
superInvestors.rationale: The Gates Foundation Trust held a concentrated ~$31.7B book (top: Berkshire, Waste Management, Canadian National, Caterpillar, Deere) with no notable individual change and no July 13D/13G filing — a low-turnover, blue-chip reference book.
superInvestors.deepDive: Included as a stable long-horizon 'permanent capital' benchmark; its concentration and inactivity contrast with the high-turnover hedge funds. Q2 13F due 14 Aug.

superInvestors.name: Trump / Trump Media (DJT)
superInvestors.rationale: Forbes pegs Trump's net worth at ~$6.1B, dominated by the ~41% DJT stake and ~$1.4B of crypto-linked lines. A 19 Jul SEC corporate update detailed Trump Media's crypto-treasury build — ~9,542 BTC (~$593M) plus a ~$2B additional BTC purchase — while Q1 loss widened to $406M on markdowns; recent DJT Form 4s are RSU grants, NOT open-market buys.
superInvestors.deepDive: The crypto exposure and DJT concentration dominate the net-worth picture, now amplified by the accelerating bitcoin-treasury strategy (~$2.6B BTC) that ties DJT's book to crypto beta — a headwind as BTC de-risked to ~$63.5k into the FOMC. The absence of any insider open-market purchase and the RSU-heavy Form 4 activity are the recent corporate developments. Disclosed prior individual buys include NVDA, AAPL and MSFT.

superInvestors.name: Bridgewater Associates
superInvestors.rationale: No new large 13D/13G or reported Bridgewater move surfaced this run beyond the Q1 book; the fund's diversified, macro-driven, ETF-heavy positioning rarely produces single-name signals. Carried pending the 14 Aug Q2 13F.
superInvestors.deepDive: Included for roster completeness; no material change verified this run (gap).

insiders.rationale: Xiaomi repurchased 3.9M Class B shares for HK$100.7M on 15 July 2026 (HKEX filing), continuing its multi-tranche buyback program alongside a strong June EV-delivery print (+36% to 34,738 units) — a company backing its own equity through HK-tech volatility.
insiders.deepDive: An issuer repurchase signals management's capital-allocation confidence rather than a single insider's bet, and Xiaomi's buyback runs in parallel with Tencent's. The corporate bid offers downside support, though Xiaomi remains a high-beta HK-tech name that swings with the HSTECH tape and still lags YTD — offering relative catch-up if the rally broadens on Politburo follow-through.

insiders.rationale: Capital Group crossed above the 5% substantial-shareholder threshold in Singtel, filing a notice showing 837,947,249 shares (5.1%) at an average ~S$4.67 — a large institutional accumulation in a core SGX holding as the STI printed record highs.
insiders.deepDive: A global institution crossing 5% in Singtel is a meaningful vote of confidence in the telco's capital-return and asset-recycling story, and it sits on top of Singtel's own S$2B Value Realisation buyback (launched 9 Jul). Substantial-shareholder notices are a cleaner institutional signal than director trades.

insiders.shares: change in interest (exact figure not captured — SGXNet PDF)
insiders.rationale: Wing Tai Holdings filed a 'Change in Interest of Director' on SGXNet dated 9 July 2026 — a fresh director-interest movement in one of the portfolio's SGX developer names (the exact share/value figures were not extractable from the SGXNet PDF this run).
insiders.deepDive: The Cheng-family-controlled developer routinely sees interest changes tied to the controlling shareholder; a fresh dated filing in a held name is a useful reference even where the granular figure is a gap. Verify direct on links.sgx.com. Among the few named-target SGX director filings verifiable this run against limited SGXNet full-text access.

insiders.rationale: Tencent repurchased ~1.1M shares for HK$500.7M on 9 July 2026 (with HK$12.7M on 8 Jul and HK$204.8M on 6 Jul), extending a near-daily buyback streak since mid-May under the ~912M-share (10%) mandate approved at the 13 May AGM.
insiders.deepDive: Tencent runs one of the largest repurchase programs in Hong Kong; the relentless daily cadence reflects a commitment to shrinking the share count and offsetting SBC dilution — a near-mechanical corporate bid underpinning the stock through the HK-tech rebound (Hang Seng reclaiming 25,000). The core HK-tech position to hold, favored over Xiaomi on relative strength.

insiders.insider: Ross R. Bhappu (with dir. Bruce D. Hansen)
insiders.rationale: Open-market cluster buying by Energy Fuels' top brass: CEO Bhappu bought 74,000 shares at $13.08 on 7 Jul (to 256,583 direct) and director Hansen 4,000 at $12.695 on 8 Jul (to 313,844). Both Form 4s accepted by SEC EDGAR 9 Jul 2026.
insiders.deepDive: Rare genuine open-market buys (not option exercises) in the portfolio's uranium/rare-earth name — management conviction at the $12.70-13.08 zone makes that band an insider-validated reference level. It remains the only confirmed insider BUYING across the portfolio's mining names this month, against heavy AI-complex insider selling elsewhere — a striking sector contrast, and a fresh anchor as rare-earth pricing eases on China's control suspension.

insiders.role: CEO & Executive Director, Mapletree Logistics Trust Mgmt
insiders.rationale: Mapletree Logistics Trust's CEO made an open-market purchase of ~100,000 units at ~S$1.91 in early July, boosting her personal holding by ~73% — a genuine director conviction buy in the S-REIT sleeve as the trust trades near multi-year lows on the higher-for-longer rate backdrop.
insiders.deepDive: Unlike an issuer buyback, a CEO's own-account open-market purchase is a direct personal-conviction signal, and a ~73% boost is meaningful. It lands with MLT under pressure from higher-for-longer rates — the CEO stepping in near the lows is an insider-validated reference level for the industrial-S-REIT complex the book holds (Mapletree PACT, Keppel REIT peers) — a bid that looks well-timed as the oil collapse eases the 10Y (~4.62%) and SGX REIT prints come in firm (Keppel DC REIT DPU +11.3%).

insiders.role: EVP & Chief Sustainability and Development Officer
insiders.rationale: Newmont's EVP sold 3,000 shares (~$277K) at $92.38 on 1 July 2026 (filed 6 July) under a Rule 10b5-1 plan dated 17 December 2025, leaving 43,315 shares — routine, pre-scheduled selling at the world's largest gold miner (a top GDX holding).
insiders.deepDive: A scheduled 10b5-1 disposal rather than a discretionary conviction sell, so the signal is muted. As the largest US-filing gold producer and a core GDX constituent, Newmont insider activity is a useful read on miner sentiment; the absence of accompanying open-market buying is consistent with a sector that already re-rated hard. Most GDX/SILJ miners are Canadian and report on SEDI, so Newmont is one of the few surfacing in SEC filings.

insiders.rationale: Hecla Mining's General Counsel had ~23,973 shares withheld for tax on RSUs that vested 22 June 2026, with the CFO seeing similar RSU vesting/withholding — equity-compensation events, not open-market trades, at a core silver miner (SILJ/GDX). Latest available Hecla Form 4.
insiders.deepDive: Routine compensation/tax-withholding transactions with low signal value, but among the few recent US Form 4 filings in the largely-Canadian silver-miner universe. Hecla is the largest US primary silver producer; no open-market buying accompanied the vesting, consistent with insiders neither chasing nor fading the silver whipsaw — relevant as silver gave back Monday's bounce to ~$57.5 into the FOMC.

insiders.rationale: DBS CEO Tan Su Shan sold 100,000 shares at S$60.12 on 15 May 2026, leaving ~1.3 million shares (0.048% of the bank), a partial profit-taking trim as the stock first pushed above S$60 — the most recent verified insider move on the SGX-listed bank (latest available).
insiders.deepDive: DBS has since pushed to fresh record highs into its 6 August results; the sale is a liquidity/diversification trim rather than a loss of confidence given Tan's sizeable retained stake. CEO sells into all-time highs are common and often tax-driven. No within-window director/substantial-shareholder change was verifiable for DBS this run; DBS continues a S$3bn buyback through 2027.
